title: removeCollateralWLpTo only checks tokenId membership on full removal; any position owner can unwrap LP / harvest rewards of wLp NFTs held by PosManager for other positions
description: Discovery: Module S (cross-contract state on transfer), mandatory cross-contract read of IBaseWrapLp. PosManager is the ERC721 owner of every collateralized wLp NFT, and wLp.unwrap/harvest are gated only by NFT ownership (onlyOwner(id)). removeCollateralWLpTo reads balanceOfLp(_tokenId) globally and only enforces ids[_wLp].remove(_tokenId) when the resulting balance is 0. Partial or zero-amount removal never ties _tokenId to _posId, so the caller's own position authorizes an unwrap/harvest of someone else's NFT. The same path is reachable from liquidateWLp: a liquidator can pass a foreign _tokenId (getCollWLpAmt returns 0 so wLpAmtToBurn = 0) and force a harvest whose rewards are credited to the liquidated position. NFTs that sit in PosManager awaiting collateralizeWLp (transfer and collateralize in separate txs) are exposed the same way.
root_cause: Authorization of the (_wLp,_tokenId) pair against _posId is placed inside the newWLpAmt == 0 branch only; the unwrap and harvest external calls run with PosManager's ownership for any token id.

harm.who: users whose wLp NFTs are collateral in their positions
harm.loses_what: all but 1 unit of the underlying LP tokens and all pending wLp rewards

exploit_trace: 1. Victim collateralizes wLp NFT N holding 1000 LP in position V.
2. Attacker owns any position A and calls decollateralizeWLp(A, wLp, N, 999, attacker).
3. onlyAuthorized(A) passes; whitelist passes; removeCollateralWLpTo computes newWLpAmt = 1 so the membership check is skipped.
4. PosManager (owner of N) harvests N (rewards credited to pendingRewards[A]) and unwraps 999 LP to the attacker.
5. ensurePositionHealth(A) checks only A, unchanged, so the call succeeds; victim's position is left with a 1-LP NFT.

preconditions.text: a whitelisted wLp NFT is held by PosManager for another position

postconditions.text: victim position undercollateralized and possibly liquidatable

depth_evidence: [BOUNDARY:_amt=0 -> newWLpAmt=balance, no membership check, harvest of foreign token]

title: updatePosDebtShares snapshots lastDebtAmt with pre-operation pool ratio; a second debt update on the same position/pool in the same timestamp underflows and reverts (can block liquidation or repay/borrow batches)
description: Discovery: Q4.x cross-contract rounding/ordering check (PosManager <-> LendingPool). InitCore calls IPosManager.updatePosDebtShares BEFORE the pool mutates (borrow/repay), so lastDebtAmt = ceil(newShares*TD/TS) uses the old totals. The pool then rounds shares up on borrow (and amount up on repay), lowering TD/TS slightly. A later update at the same timestamp (no interest accrued) computes debtAmtCurrent from the new ratio, which can be 1 wei below lastDebtAmt, so `debtAmtCurrent - extraInfo.lastDebtAmt` underflows (0.8.19 checked arithmetic) and the call reverts. A random-parameter simulation of one borrow followed by a second update gave a lower debtAmtCurrent in about 29% of cases.
root_cause: The snapshot is taken from stale pool totals before the pool applies the rounded-up share/amount change, and the next update assumes debtAmtCurrent >= lastDebtAmt without a guard.

harm.loses_what: ability to liquidate/repay/borrow in the affected timestamp (liquidation of an unhealthy position can be blocked by a borrower who touches the same pool in the same block)

exploit_trace: 1. Position P owes shares S in pool X with TD/TS != 1; owner borrows a small amount (or repays) in block B: lastDebtAmt snapshotted with the old ratio, then pool rounds up.
2. In the same block (same timestamp) a liquidator's liquidate() runs _repay -> updatePosDebtShares(P, X, -s).
3. debtShareToAmtCurrent now returns a value below lastDebtAmt, so the subtraction underflows and liquidate reverts.
4. Borrower repeats a dust borrow/repay each block ahead of liquidators; the same revert also hits borrow+borrow or repay+borrow batches on one pool.

preconditions.text: two debt updates on one position/pool at the same block.timestamp with a rounding mismatch

postconditions.text: liquidation of the position fails for that timestamp

title: MoneyMarketHook pulls repay tokens for the requested shares but core repays only min(shares, position debt); excess is stranded in the hook and stealable for WNATIVE
description: Discovery: Q2 value-in vs value-out cross-contract check (hook vs core). The hook computes repayAmt = debtShareToAmtCurrent(_params[i].shares) and pulls that from the user, but InitCore._repay clamps sharesToRepay to the position's actual debt shares and transfers only that amount from the hook. If the position's debt shares dropped between signing and execution (partial liquidation front-run, or the user overshooting to close a debt), the difference stays in the hook. No refund exists. For WNATIVE, returnNative=true unwraps the hook's whole WNATIVE balance and sends the whole ETH balance to the next caller; other tokens are stuck permanently.
root_cause: The hook sizes the pull from caller-supplied shares instead of min(shares, position debt shares) and never refunds leftovers.

harm.loses_what: the overpaid amount (stuck, or taken by whoever next calls execute with returnNative for WNATIVE)
harm.magnitude: difference between requested and actual repaid debt

exploit_trace: 1. User calls hook.execute with repay shares = full debt of a WNATIVE pool position.
2. A liquidator's tx lands first and reduces the position's debt shares.
3. Hook pulls WNATIVE for the full requested shares; core repays only the remaining shares; excess WNATIVE stays in the hook.
4. Attacker calls execute with posId = 0, a valid mode and returnNative = true; the hook unwraps its WNATIVE balance and pays all ETH to the attacker.

preconditions.text: requested repay shares exceed position debt shares at execution

depth_evidence: [VARIATION:shares=S vs debt=S-x -> x excess in hook]

title: MoneyMarketHook pre-transfers deposits to the pool before the multicall; a repay or second deposit on the same pool absorbs them into cash so mintTo reverts with ZERO_VALUE
description: Discovery: Module T (intra-batch balance deltas). Deposit tokens are sent to the pool during hook preparation, before the core multicall runs. LendingPool.repay sets cash = balanceOf(pool), so a repay on the same pool earlier in the multicall folds the pending deposit into cash. The later mintTo computes amt = balanceOf - cash = 0 and reverts with ZERO_VALUE. Two deposit params for the same pool fail the same way, because the first mintTo absorbs both transfers.
root_cause: Balance-delta accounting in the pool plus transfers staged outside the multicall ordering.

harm.who: hook users batching repay + deposit on the same asset
harm.loses_what: the batched call always reverts (liveness only, no fund loss); users must split calls

exploit_trace: 1. User calls execute with repayParams[pool X] and depositParams[pool X].
2. Prep phase moves the repay tokens to the hook and the deposit tokens to pool X.
3. Multicall repay: core moves repay tokens to X; pool.repay sets cash = balanceOf(X), including the deposit.
4. mintTo(X, POS_MANAGER): amt = 0, shares = 0, revert ZERO_VALUE.

preconditions.text: repay and deposit (or two deposits) target the same pool in one execute

title: Liquidation of a position with health == 0 reverts with division by zero in LiqIncentiveCalculator despite InitCore's underwater bypass
description: Discovery: cross-contract read of the incentive calculator called from liquidate/liquidateWLp. health_e18 == 0 (collateral credit 0 with debt > 0, e.g. after earlier liquidation seized all collateral, or collFactor 0) is handled as a valid underwater case by InitCore, but it is first passed to getLiqIncentiveMultiplier_e18, which divides ONE_E18*ONE_E18 by _healthFactor_e18 and panics. Residual bad debt of fully seized positions can therefore never be liquidated or repaid via liquidation.
root_cause: Callee assumes health > 0; caller treats 0 as valid.

harm.loses_what: underwater positions with zero collateral credit cannot be liquidated; bad debt stays accruing

exploit_trace: 1. Position has debt and zero collateral credit, so getPosHealthCurrent_e18 returns 0.
2. Liquidator calls liquidate(); _liquidateInternal passes the < 1e18 check and repays.
3. getLiqIncentiveMultiplier_e18(mode, 0, ...) divides by zero and the call reverts.

preconditions.text: collateral credit equals zero while debt is non-zero

title: InitOracle try/catch does not cover an unset (address(0)) source, so the documented single-source fallback reverts
description: Discovery: oracle-analysis module (fallback integrity). The comments promise that a single valid source is used when the other is invalid. A high-level call to address(0) fails the extcodesize check inside InitOracle, which a try/catch does not catch, so any token with only a primary (or only a secondary) source configured always reverts instead of using the configured one. A source that returns malformed data reverts at ABI decoding in the caller in the same way.
root_cause: try/catch only handles reverts raised inside the callee, not the caller-side extcodesize and decode checks.

harm.who: borrowers and liquidators of tokens with one configured source
harm.loses_what: price reads revert, blocking borrow, withdraw and liquidation for that token

exploit_trace: 1. Governor configures only a primary source for token T (secondary = address(0)).
2. Any call that prices T reaches the secondary try; the extcodesize check reverts, uncaught.
3. Health checks, borrows and liquidations involving T revert.

preconditions.text: one of the two sources is unset or returns malformed data
